historicalReference.compiler: Main native release defaults: thin LTO, eight codegen units, no PGO or added target-cpu flags. The optimized reference uses its production native/fat-LTO/PGO build; speedup includes engine, allocator and compiler differences.

findings: Copying only old tactics into the optimized engine would silently accelerate old helpers and allocator operations. The complete source and catalog are frozen instead.
Per-game IPC was 5–14% faster than historical chooser timing. A dedicated simulation thread repaired most Rush cost but not Classic. Overlapping IPC made chooser costs higher.

The final integration runs the original execution and recording path to completion before importing records. Against a fresh frozen-binary run, Classic/Rush/Mixed chooser CPU differs by -0.13%, +0.30% and -1.07%.

The historical Classic mean was 109.49 microseconds; rerunning the unchanged frozen binary measured 117.78. Historical wall/CPU timings are observations, not deterministic equality requirements. Every gameplay field, decision count, turn count and cap count is exact.
limits: Native complete-match comparison entrants only; old-versus-old battles and campaigns supported. Live/WASM planner continuations and cross-version opponents rejected.
Old whole-command wall time includes original JSONL recording plus Arrow import and cannot be compared directly with current engine wall time. Actual chooser/phase CPU excludes import.
All eight can be compared in one arena report with --self-play --profile-turns and --data-dir rust/legacy/data.
